The amount of heat required to convert the state of matter at a constant temperature is called the

latent heat of the matter. The latent heat during the change of state from solid to liquid or viceversa is called the latent heat of fusion. The latent heat during the change of state from liquid to gas or vice-versa is called the latent heat of vaporization. Latent heat is called so because it is hidden from the thermometer reading. Latent heat is also called heat of transformation.

During the change of state of a matter, heat is used for two purposes;one to overcome the external atmospheric pressure to create a space for expansion, and the next to reduce the intermolecular force of attraction. The former is called external latent heat and latter is called internal latent heat. External latent heat is much smaller than internal latent heat. Value of both types of heat are much greater in case of conversion of state from liquid to gas than that in the case of conversion of state from solid to liquid. Therefore, the latent heat of vaporization is always greater than the latent heat of fusion.

Latent heat cannot be measured in terms of change in velocity and change in kinetic energy of molecules. But, energy can neither be created nor can it be destroyed. Hence, during the change of phase, heat is used to increase potential energy molecules but not kinetic energy. Therefore, heat can also be considered as potential energy.
